page.title: TrueNAS Backup Destinations
page.subtitle: Back up containers to a TrueNAS instance via WebDAV (RFC 4918). TrueNAS exposes WebDAV on the share's configured path (default /webdav for the standard WebDAV share). Operators authenticate with a local TrueNAS user + password over HTTP Basic auth. Chunked uploads use Content-Range PUT, supported server-side by the TrueNAS Samba server.
page.registerHint: Click Test connection to verify the WebDAV endpoint is reachable and the credentials are valid.

form.hostHelp: Base URL of the TrueNAS server, e.g. https://nas.local. Do not add a trailing slash.
form.usernameHelp: Local TrueNAS user. The user must have read/write access to the configured WebDAV share.
form.passwordHelp: Password for the local TrueNAS user. Stored encrypted at rest by the host's AES-256-GCM service.
form.basePathHelp: Optional subfolder under the share's WebDAV root. Leave blank for the share root.
form.apiPathHelp: Override the WebDAV path. Defaults to /webdav. Operators with multiple WebDAV shares can set this to /webdav/{share-name}.
form.introBody: TrueNAS uses a local user account for WebDAV authentication. The user must have read/write access to the configured WebDAV share. McHarbor stores the password encrypted at rest.

setup.title: TrueNAS setup guide
setup.step1: On the TrueNAS side, create a WebDAV share: Services → SMB → add a share. Set the path to a directory you want backups to land in (e.g. /mnt/tank/backups). TrueNAS exposes the share at /webdav by default once the WebDAV service is enabled (Services → SMB → advanced settings or via the WebDAV-specific service on newer versions).
setup.step2: Create a local TrueNAS user (or use an existing one) with read/write access to the share's directory. The user's home directory doesn't matter — only the share's ACL does.
setup.step3: In McHarbor, paste the TrueNAS base URL (e.g. https://nas.local — no trailing slash), the username, and the user's password into the form on the left. Optional: set a subfolder under the share's WebDAV root (e.g. Backups/2026) and let McHarbor create intermediate folders automatically.
setup.step4: Click Test connection to round-trip a probe file in the resolved folder. The plugin performs an HTTP Basic-authenticated WebDAV PROPFIND against /webdav to confirm the destination is reachable and the credentials are valid.
setup.step5: For multi-share setups, set the WebDAV path override (e.g. /webdav/Backups) to point at the share's path under the WebDAV root.
setup.step6: Trigger a backup. The plugin uploads the archive via WebDAV using Content-Range chunked PUT. TrueNAS's samba.org-based WebDAV server supports chunked uploads so even 10+ GB backups stream without buffering the entire payload in memory at once.
